title: fix(discord): prevent other members from disrupting voice connections
body:
Fixes #172648

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord voice joins timing out, reconnecting muted, or switching channels when another guild member changes voice state.

## User Impact

Other members joining, leaving, moving, or changing mute/deaf settings no longer overwrite the bot's voice connection state. Participant rosters, occupancy-based auto-join, and follow-user behavior still receive those events. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord Gateway now records the bot user ID from `READY` and forwards only that member's voice-state packets to the adapter registered for the packet's guild. Voice-server updates have no user ID and continue to route by guild. This replaces the single-caller forwarding helper and removes its generic guild reader, reducing production code by 11 lines.

The adapter lookup and identity check happen synchronously in the Gateway owner before listener dispatch; this adds no detached or deferred effects and captures no stale authority, config, identity, session binding, path, or limit for later use.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirms the defect on main at `69d500b410f5d2f6ad169b9852f4d2c28cc720e0`: all guild members reached the adapter, whose dependency overwrites session identity and connection settings from each packet.
- Regression: `routes only the bot's own guild voice updates to its adapter while preserving other members' events` in `extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`. It uses the real socket dispatch, Client, and VoicePlugin with synthetic wire events, covering own join/leave, foreign join/move/leave, differing mute/deaf/session values, guild isolation for both event types, and roster/listener delivery.
- Local changed-file oxlint (`--config .oxlintrc.json`) and oxfmt checks passed; `git diff --check` passed. The package-preparing lint wrapper was stopped; the changed-file core-config lint route was used instead.
- Deslop completed. Isolated Codex autoreview through P2, including the CI follow-up: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- PR CI is the test and typecheck gate, including the Discord Gateway regression and affected plugin/sibling suites. Local tests, test timing, typechecks, and production-revert negative control were intentionally deferred under maintainer policy.
- Live Gateway proof, Crabbox, and Testbox were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy; no leases or live Gateway processes were created.

The first CI run [38659691090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659691090) passed the regression in 19 ms and its Discord shard (217 tests in 22 files; 45.72 s). The only reported failure was [assertion-safety job 116178188039](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38659691090/job/116178188039): deleting `readGuildId` removed two assertions, so its per-file allowance needed to shrink from 7 to 5. That exact entry is now updated; no exceptions were added. After merging current main, [final-head Discord CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660851241/job/116181906899) passed the regression in 10 ms and all 217 tests in 22 files (29.17 s) at `10a96e28e5c02f638c63d9bbd6873942516b81b6`. [Final-head CI run 38660851241](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38660851241) completed successfully: all 36 executed jobs passed, including production/test typechecks, lint, docs, boundaries, and the corrected assertion ratchet.
